subject: math-aa-hl

title: Skew lines and a minimum distance
stem: $L_1:\mathbf r=(t,0,0)$ and $L_2:\mathbf r=(0,1+u,1-u)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Prove that the lines are skew.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: By minimizing the squared distance between general points on the lines, find their minimum distance.

steps.text: Their directions (1,0,0) and (0,1,−1) are not parallel.
An intersection would require 1+u=0 and 1−u=0 simultaneously.
These conditions are inconsistent, so nonparallel, nonintersecting lines are skew.
The minimum squared distance is 2, attained at t=u=0.

stem: For $t\ge0$, particles have positions $\mathbf a(t)=(t,2t,1)$ and $\mathbf b(t)=(4-t,t,1)$. Distances are in metres and t is in seconds.

title: A cone, its net and an inscribed sphere
stem: A right circular cone has base radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. A sphere touches the base and the curved surface internally.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the angle, in radians, of the sector forming the curved-surface net.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the sphere radius, deriving the needed relation from a central cross-section.

steps.text: The sector arc length equals the base circumference, 12π.
Let the sphere radius be r. Its centre is 8−r from the apex along the axis.
The half-apex angle α has $\sin\alpha=6/10$; tangency requires $r=(8-r)\sin\alpha$.

title: A cyclic quadrilateral fixes its diagonal
stem: A cyclic quadrilateral ABCD has side lengths AB=3, BC=4, CD=5 and DA=6. The diagonal AC has length x.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use the cosine rule in the two triangles to find x exactly.

parts.label: b

steps.text: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $\pi$, so $\cos D=-\cos B$.
